answer: Practically, the chain should make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because vault only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, anchor is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any grove approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
